facts: $8^{3}$ is read '$8$ to the power of $3$' and stands for $8\times 8\times 8$.
**Index**, **power** and **exponent** all mean the same thing.
The base is the number being multiplied; the index counts how many times it appears.
A number written with no index has an index of $1$, so $6=6^{1}$.
Writing the repeated multiplication out in full is called **expanded form**.
steps: Count how many times each factor appears.
Write each factor as a base with that count as its index.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) In $11^{4}$, name the base and the index, then say how it is read.
(b) Write $13$ in index form, showing its index.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) The base is $11$ and the index is $4$.
It is read '$11$ to the power of $4$'.
The index is also called the power or exponent.
(b) A number without a written index has an index of $1$.
$13=13^{1}$

workedExamples.question_text:
Write each product in index form. For (b), put the smaller base first.
(a) $9\times9\times9\times9$
(b) $13\times17\times13\times13\times17$
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) There are four factors of $9$.
$9\times9\times9\times9=9^{4}$
(b) Group the equal factors together.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}13\times17\times13\times13\times17\\&=(13\times13\times13)\times(17\times17)\\&=13^{3}\times17^{2}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Write $7^{2}\times11^{4}$ in expanded form. How many numbers are multiplied together altogether, and how many of them are $11$?
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}7^{2}\times11^{4}\\&=(7\times7)\times(11\times11\times11\times11)\end{aligned}$
There are $2+4=6$ numbers multiplied together.
Four of them are $11$.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Write $5\times5\times5\times5\times5\times5$ in index form using base $5$, then using base $25$.
(b) Sam writes $7\times7\times11\times11\times11$ as $77^{5}$. Is Sam correct? Write the correct index form.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) There are six factors of $5$.
$5\times5\times5\times5\times5\times5=5^{6}$
Group them in pairs.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}5^{6}\\&=(5\times5)\times(5\times5)\times(5\times5)\\&=25\times25\times25\\&=25^{3}\end{aligned}$
(b)
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}7\times7\times11\times11\times11\\&=(7\times7)\times(11\times11\times11)\\&=7^{2}\times11^{3}\end{aligned}$
Sam is not correct. $77^{5}$ would mean five factors of $77$, or five pairs of $7\times11$. The given product has only two $7$s and three $11$s.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Write $(-6)\times(-6)\times(-6)$ in index form.
(b) Write $5^{2}\times\left(\frac{3}{7}\right)^{3}$ in expanded form.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) The repeated base is $-6$. Keep it inside brackets.
$(-6)\times(-6)\times(-6)=(-6)^{3}$
(b) Repeat each whole base the number of times shown by its index.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}5^{2}\times\left(\frac{3}{7}\right)^{3}\\&=(5\times5)\times\left(\frac{3}{7}\times\frac{3}{7}\times\frac{3}{7}\right)\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Write $11\times3\times11\times2\times3\times11$ in index form, with the bases in increasing order. State the index of the factor $2$.
(b) Find the missing index: $7\times7\times7\times7\times13\times13=7^{\square}\times13^{2}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Group the equal factors and count each group.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}11\times3\times11\times2\times3\times11\\&=2\times(3\times3)\times(11\times11\times11)\\&=2\times3^{2}\times11^{3}\end{aligned}$
The factor $2$ appears once, so its index is $1$.
(b) There are four factors of $7$ and two factors of $13$.
$7\times7\times7\times7\times13\times13=7^{4}\times13^{2}$
The missing index is $4$.

foundation.question_text: Name the base and the index in $7^{5}$.
foundation.solution_text:
$7^{5}$
The base is $7$ and the index is $5$.

development.question_text: Write $6\times 3\times 6\times 3\times 6\times 3$ in index form, with the smaller base first.
Write $4\times 13\times 4\times 4\times 7$ in index form, with the bases in increasing order.
State the base and the index of each power in $2^{5}\times 7$.
development.solution_text:
$2^{5}\times 7$
$=2^{5}\times 7^{1}$
The first power has base $2$ and index $5$; the second has base $7$ and index $1$.
